summary: No security findings. Trust boundary (REQ-025): recommendPostflop and recommend take only a PlayerView (src/engine/player-view.ts), whose PublicPlayer type carries no hole cards and which has no deck field. The equity input is built only from view.holeCards, view.board and opponent ranges that are every combo not containing hero or board cards (unseenCombos). It never reads earlierShowdowns or any engine state. The injectable options.equity function gets exactly that same EquityInput, so no injected function can receive hidden information through this path. The option is a caller-supplied test seam, not an untrusted input. Resource bounds: there is one computeEquity call per recommendation. The opponent count is at most 9 live non-hero seats, and computeEquity rejects anything outside 1..MAX_OPPONENTS=9. The work is capped by EXACT_EVALUATION_LIMIT=200,000, otherwise SAMPLE_TRIALS=30,000 with FEASIBILITY_NODE_LIMIT and a rejection cap. unseenCombos builds at most 1,326 combos. The 9-opponent range array reuses one shared array instead of 9 copies. No unbounded loop exists. The AC#5 test reads two fixed repo-relative paths, 'docs/advice/postflop-rules.md' and 'tests/advice/postflop.test.ts', joined to REPO_ROOT with no variable input, so there is no traversal. The change adds no dependencies and has no secrets, logging, network, env, eval or filesystem access in src. Randomness stays the existing seeded sampler, which is fine for advice (dealing fairness does not depend on it).
